releases.name: v0.41.0
releases.body:
### Breaking Changes

- **`@agent-browser/eve` tools now come from the MCP tool catalog.** The extension exposes the CLI's MCP tools instead of 21 hand-written ones, so tool names and inputs change: `navigate` is `open`, `evaluate` is `eval`, `press_key` is `press`, `select_option` is `select`, `set_checked` is `check` and `uncheck`, `get` is `get_text`, `get_url` and the other `get_*` tools, `tabs` is the `tab_*` tools, and `wait_for` is the `wait_*` tools. The same names apply to `@agent-browser/eve/tools` overrides. The sandbox needs agent-browser 0.41, which the extension installs by default (#2241)

### New Features

- Added **`agent-browser mcp call <tool> '<json>'`** to run one MCP tool without a stdio session and print its result as JSON with the agent-browser version, for runtimes that cannot keep a process open between tool calls (#2238)
- Added **`@agent-browser/sandbox/mcp-tools.json`**, every MCP tool with its title, description, input schema, annotations and profiles, generated from the CLI and checked by a test (#2240)

### Improvements

- **`@agent-browser/eve` runs each tool as its own short-lived process**, so no `agent-browser` process outlives a tool call. The 28 `core` tools are listed to the model and the other 14 are deferred, found with `eve__search`, which keeps the listed tool context at its previous size (#2241)

### Bug Fixes

- **MCP tool arguments can no longer set global flags.** The CLI reads global flags anywhere in its arguments, so a value such as a selector or `extraArgs` entry could carry its own `--allowed-domains` and override the server or caller allowlist. Tool calls that try are now rejected (#2238)

### Contributors

- @Railly
- @lahfir

activity.title: test(settings): make policy path assertions portable across platforms
activity.body:
## Description

Fixes Windows CI failures in the Rust (windows-latest - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) test suite:
- session_settings::tests::security_view
- session_settings::tests::legacy_policy_variable_applies_only_when_the_current_one_is_unset

### Root Cause
When seeding policy paths (via AGENT_BROWSER_ACTION_POLICY or AGENT_BROWSER_POLICY), Running::from_lookup converts the path using crate::flags::absolute_policy_path(&path, &cwd).
On Windows runners, cwd.join("/policy.json") resolves using the current working drive (e.g. D:/policy.json), while the tests were asserting literal equality with Some("/policy.json").

### Fix
Construct the expected path dynamically against current_dir(), making the tests portable across both Unix and Windows.

Signed-off-by: ab-rar-6024 <samohamedabrar2005@gmail.com>

activity.title: fix(policy): require evaluate for javascript: URL navigation
activity.body:
Fixes #2172

A daemon `navigate` request with a `javascript:` URL runs script in the current page, but the action policy only checks `navigate`. With `"deny": ["evaluate"]`, `eval` is denied while `navigate` to `javascript:document.title='x'` still changes the page.

## Changes

- `policy_actions_for_command` adds `evaluate` to the checked policy actions when `navigate`, `tab_new`, `a11y`, or `vitals` receives a URL whose scheme is `javascript`. This follows the existing pattern that adds `navigate` for `a11y <url>`.
- The scheme check uses `url::Url::parse`, so mixed case and leading whitespace (`" JavaScript:..."`) are covered the same way Chrome parses them.
- Other URLs are unchanged: `https://example.com/javascript:` still checks only `navigate`.

## Tests

- New unit test `test_javascript_url_policy_actions_include_evaluate` covers all four actions with lowercase and mixed-case/whitespace `javascript:` URLs, plus an `https` URL that must not require `evaluate`.
- `cd cli && cargo test --bin agent-browser javascript_url_policy`: fails without the change, passes with it.
- `cargo fmt -- --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean.

activity.title: Same-site, cross-origin iframe (in-process): refs report "outside the viewport" and frame selectors find nothing
activity.body:
## Summary A cross-origin iframe that shares the page's site (same scheme and registrable domain, different port or subdomain) is not isolated into its own process. agent-browser 0.41.2 can see its elements but cannot act on them: 1. `click @ref` on an element inside the frame fails with `Element '@eN' is outside the viewport, so the click would not reach it` whenever the element's position on the page lies beyond the frame's own width or height (any frame placed lower on the page than its own height), even though the element is in plain view. 2. `frame ""` reports `✓ Done` and `snapshot -i` then lists the frame's elements, but every selector-based command (`click "#inner"`, `get text "#state"`) fails with `Element not found in the selected frame`, and refs from that snapshot fail as in 1. A cross-**site** iframe on the same page (an OOPIF) is fine: its refs click correctly (thanks to #925). Its `frame ""` failure is already #1696, so it is not re-reported here. Version: 0.41.2, macOS arm64, HeadlessChrome 152 launched by agent-browser. Also seen on CEF 154 attached with `--cdp`. ## Reproduction `a/index.html`, served on port 8471: ```html

Page A

``` `b/frame.html`, served on port 8472: ```html

frame idle

``` ```bash (cd a && python3 -m http.server 8471) & (cd b && python3 -m http.server 8472) & agent-browser open http://localhost:8471/index.html # same site as the frame: in-process agent-browser snapshot -i agent-browser click @e3 # the "Inner button" ref agent-browser frame "#frame" agent-browser click "#inner" ``` ## Observed ``` - heading "Page A" [level=1, ref=e1] - Iframe [ref=e2] - button "Inner button" [ref=e3] ✗ Element '@e3' is outside the viewport, so the click would not reach it ✓ Done ✗ Element not found in the selected frame: #inner. Verify the selector, role, or name is correct and the element exists in the DOM. ``` Opening the parent as `http://127.0.0.1:8471/index.html` instead makes the frame cross-site, and clicking the button's ref then succeeds (the frame's text becomes `frame clicked`). Without the 400px spacer the in-process click also succeeds, because the button's page coordinates happen to fall inside the frame's 400×200. Launching Chrome with `--enable-features=StrictOriginIsolation` also makes the in-process case succeed, since the frame then gets its own process. ## Expected The frame's elements can be clicked by ref and addressed by selector after `frame`, as they are when the frame is cross-site. ## Likely cause Both paths walk up with `defaultView.frameElement` or read `contentDocument`, and both are `null` when the frame and its parent are cross-origin, even though they share a renderer process and a CDP session: - `check_node_interception` (`cli/src/native/element.rs`, around line 643) climbs `topDoc.defaultView.frameElement` to reach the top document. For a cross-origin, in-process frame the loop stops at once, so `ACTIONABILITY_JS` runs against the frame's own document with top-level box-model coordinates. Its `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` are the frame's (400×200), the point is outside them, and `elementFromPoint` in the frame's document finds nothing, so it answers `outside the viewport`. The comment above it assumes the walk only stops at a process boundary, which does not hold for a same-site frame. - The frame-scoped lookup (around line 338) starts from `this.contentDocument`, which is `null` for a cross-origin frame, so nothing is ever found inside it. A fix probably needs to resolve such frames by frame id, as the OOPIF path does (`DOM.getFrameOwner`, then an isolated world or execution context for that frame through `Page.createIsolatedWorld`), rather than relying on DOM access across the origin boundary.

activity.title: Windows: cold first `open` can fail with "os error 10060" after 30s while Chrome is still launching
activity.body:
On Windows, the very first `open` of a fresh session can fail after exactly 30 seconds with a misleading socket error, even when Chrome is installed and the page loads:

```
✗ Failed to read: ... (os error 10060) (the command reached the daemon but no response came back; it may or may not have run, so it was not retried)
```

A `get url` a few seconds later returns the page URL, so the open did succeed. The error comes from the CLI's 30s read timeout firing while the daemon is still launching Chrome on a cold start, and it reads like a network problem with the target site.

Seen on main (0.41.1) on a `windows-latest` GitHub Actions runner, Git Bash, Chrome 156, on 1 of 2 cold starts.

Expected: a cold first launch either finishes within the read timeout, or reports that the browser launch is still in progress (or timed out) instead of a raw `os error 10060`.

Related: #1711 (the original missing-Chrome case, which main now reports as "Chrome not found").

activity.title: click, eval, and screenshot on a stuck tab report os error 35 instead of page_wedged
activity.body:
When the active tab stops responding, read-only commands such as `snapshot` report `page_wedged` and then say the tab was replaced by a blank one. Commands that can change the page, such as `click`, `eval`, and `screenshot`, report only `Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)`. The tab is still replaced, but the caller is never told, so the next command runs on `about:blank` with no warning.

## Repro

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser eval 'setTimeout(()=>{while(true){}},50); 1'
agent-browser wait 300
agent-browser click p        # or: eval 1, or screenshot /tmp/x.png
agent-browser click p
agent-browser eval location.href
```

| Command | First call | Second call |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot`, `get text body` | 33 s, `✗ page_wedged: the active tab stopped responding; …` | 36 s, `✗ page_wedged: … was replaced by a blank tab; navigate again to continue` |
| `click p`, `eval 1`, `screenshot` | 30 s, `✗ Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35) (the command reached the daemon but no response came back; …)` | 36 s, the same os error 35 |

After either sequence the tab is `about:blank`. For `click`, `eval`, and `screenshot`, the `page_wedged` report and the blank-tab warning appear to go out on a socket the CLI has already stopped reading, after its 30 s read timeout.

## Expected

`click`, `eval`, and `screenshot` report `page_wedged` the way `snapshot` does, and the caller learns that the tab was replaced. Either the daemon's wedge check could finish inside the CLI's read window for every command, or the CLI could wait as long for these commands as it does for read-only ones.

On 0.27.0 the same page left the session stuck for good, with every later command failing after 152 s. Since #2100 the session recovers, so this report is only about what the caller is told.

Related: #2100, #2085.

Environment: agent-browser 0.41.0, Chrome for Testing 150.0.7871.24, macOS 27.2 arm64, browser launched by agent-browser (no `--cdp`), headless.

---
Investigated and filed by Claude (Claude Code) on behalf of @ianb.

activity.title: Remove rsid attributes from all XML elements in document.xml
activity.body:
### Description

Currently, the `_strip_rsid_attrs()` function removes revision identifier (`rsid`) attributes only from `<w:r>` elements in `word/document.xml`. However, Microsoft Word also stores revision identifiers on other XML elements, including paragraphs (`<w:p>`), tables (`<w:tbl>`), and section properties (`<w:sectPr>`).

As a result, revision identifiers can remain in the document even after the merging process completes.

This change updates `_strip_rsid_attrs()` to recursively traverse the entire XML document and remove all attributes whose names contain `rsid`, regardless of the element on which they appear.

### Changes Made

- Modified `_strip_rsid_attrs()` to accept the XML root element instead of a list of runs.
- Implemented recursive traversal of all XML elements.
- Removed matching `rsid` attributes from every element in the document.
- Added a counter to track the number of removed attributes.
- Updated the function call in `merge_runs()` to pass the document root.

### Benefits

- Ensures more comprehensive cleanup of revision metadata.
- Removes revision identifiers from paragraphs, tables, section properties, and other XML elements.
- Improves consistency of the document cleanup process.
- Maintains the existing run-merging functionality without changing the document's rendered appearance.

### Scope

This modification affects only `word/document.xml`. Other DOCX components, including headers, footers, and footnotes, remain unaffected.

### Testing

The updated implementation should be verified against documents containing `rsid` attributes on multiple XML element types, ensuring that all matching attributes are removed and that the resulting DOCX remains valid and renders correctly.

activity.title: slack-gif-creator: make emoji mode actually reduce to 12 frames
activity.body:
Fixes #1813.

Emoji mode in `GIFBuilder.save()` says it's reducing frames to ~12, but the stride was `len(self.frames) // 12`. That's 1 for anything between 13 and 23 frames, so it printed the message and kept every frame. For counts that aren't a multiple of 12 the stride came out too small and you'd end up over the target (25 -> 13, 35 -> 18, 47 -> 16).

Since the skill tells people to keep emoji GIFs under 3s at 10 fps, 13-29 frames is exactly where most emoji GIFs land, and only 24 was actually getting reduced.

The fix picks 12 evenly spaced frames (`i * n // 12`), which is how `optimize_colors()` already samples frames a few lines up. For multiples of 12 that's the same index list as the old `range(0, n, n // 12)`, so those outputs don't change.

### Testing

Built GIFs at 128x128 / 10 fps with distinct frames, saved with `optimize_for_emoji=True`, and counted frames in the written file with Pillow:

| frames in | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 11 / 12 | 11 / 12 | 11 / 12 |
| 13, 17, 20, 23 | 13, 17, 20, 23 | 12 |
| 25, 27, 29 | 13, 14, 15 | 12 |
| 35, 47 | 18, 16 | 12 |
| 24, 36, 48 | 12 | 12 |

Also checked:
- 24, 36, 48, 60, 120 frames produce byte-identical GIFs before and after
- `optimize_for_emoji=False` produces byte-identical GIFs before and after (13, 20, 30 frames)
- 480x480 input still resizes to 128x128 and then reduces 20 -> 12
- for every n from 13 to 399 the sampled indices start at 0, strictly increase and stay in range

One thing to be aware of: frames still use `1000 / fps` as their delay, so a 20-frame input now plays in 1.2s instead of 2.0s. That's the same thing that already happens for 24+ frames today, so I left timing alone here.

activity.title: remotion-best-practices: Invalid skill structure with .yaml and .svg files
activity.body:
## Problem

The `remotion-best-practices` skill (version a2824c6) contains files that violate the Agent Skills specification:

- `remotion-license/agents/openai.yaml`
- `remotion-license/assets/remotion-icon.svg`

According to the skill audit system, skills should only contain Markdown files (*.md). These additional files:

1. **Prevent installation** - The skill auditor blocks installation due to invalid file types
2. **Cannot be verified** - YAML and SVG files are not auditable like Markdown instructions
3. **Create security risk** - Non-documentation files could potentially inject configuration or code
4. **Break the specification** - Violates the public repository for Agent Skills structure

## Expected behavior

The skill should contain only Markdown documentation files, no configuration files or assets.

## Current behavior

- `remotion-best-practices` cannot be installed due to invalid file types
- Users receive: `ERROR: auditoría con hallazgos: no se instaló nada`
- Files in invalid format are present in the upstream version

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `~/.claude/scripts/skill-update.sh review remotion-best-practices`
2. Observe the audit failure about .yaml and .svg files

## Solution

Remove or relocate the following files from the skill:
- `src/skills/remotion-best-practices/remotion-license/agents/openai.yaml`
- `src/skills/remotion-best-practices/remotion-license/assets/remotion-icon.svg`

activity.title: skill-creator: run_eval.py parallel workers cross-match skill UUIDs, producing false-negative trigger rates
activity.body:
## Summary

`skills/skill-creator/scripts/run_eval.py` produces **systematically wrong (near-zero) trigger rates whenever `--num-workers > 1`** (the default is 10). The failure is silent: every query — including ones that obviously *should* trigger — comes back with `trigger_rate ≈ 0`, which then makes all `should_trigger: false` cases "pass" trivially and all `should_trigger: true` cases "fail". The aggregate looks like a bad skill description when in fact the *measurement* is broken.

## Root cause

`run_single_query` writes each query's temp command file into a **shared** project commands dir and runs every `claude -p` in the **same** project:

```python
clean_name = f"{skill_name}-skill-{unique_id}"          # line ~52  (per-query UUID)
project_commands_dir = Path(project_root) / ".claude" / "commands"   # line ~53  (SHARED)
command_file = project_commands_dir / f"{clean_name}.md"
...
cwd=project_root,                                        # line ~89  (SHARED)
```

Detection then requires the model's invoked skill name to contain **this query's** UUID:

```python
if clean_name in accumulated_json:   # line ~147
    return True
...
return clean_name in accumulated_json   # line ~152
```

With `ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers)` (line ~198) running ~10 queries concurrently, up to ~10 command files — **identical descriptions, different UUIDs** — coexist in the shared `.claude/commands/` dir. Each `claude -p` sees all of them and invokes *one* fleet of the skill, but the per-query check only matches *its own* UUID. The model almost always triggers a sibling worker's UUID → the query records a false negative. Result: trigger rate collapses to ~0 across the board.

## Reproduction / evidence

Running the same 12-query trigger set against the same skill + description, only changing `--num-workers`:

| Run | `--num-workers` | Result |
|-----|-----------------|--------|
| Parallel (default) | 12 | **0/12 queries triggered** — even a query literally starting `"Fleet tune the GET /api/board endpoint…"` against a description containing the phrase `fleet tune` returned 0/3. All negatives "passed" only because nothing fired. |
| Serial | 1 | **10/12 correct** — clean signal: 4/6 positives fire, 6/6 negatives correctly stay off. |

Manually invoking one obvious positive with a single command file present shows the model's **first tool call is `Skill(<the skill>)`** — i.e. triggering works; only the parallel measurement is broken.

## Fix

Isolate each query in its own project dir so a `claude -p` only ever sees its own command file:

```python
import tempfile, shutil
iso_root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="trigeval-"))
project_commands_dir = iso_root / ".claude" / "commands"
command_file = project_commands_dir / f"{clean_name}.md"
try:
    project_commands_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    command_file.write_text(command_content)
    # ... Popen(..., cwd=str(iso_root), env=env)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(iso_root, ignore_errors=True)
```

This removes the cross-matching entirely (each worker's `clean_name` is the only skill in its tree) and lets parallel runs stay fast and correct.

## Workaround until then

Pass `--num-workers 1` to `run_eval.py` / `run_loop.py`. Note `run_loop.py` forwards `--num-workers` to `run_eval`, so the same bug silently corrupts the optimization signal at the default of 10 — every iteration optimizes against ~0 trigger rates.

Found while triggering-testing a new skill; happy to send a PR with the isolation fix if useful.

activity.title: Fix console-window popups from skill helper subprocesses on Windows (CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
activity.body:
## Summary

Helper scripts across the docx / pptx / xlsx / skill-creator / webapp-testing skills spawn child processes (`soffice`, `recalc.py`, dev servers, eval runners, redlining validators, thumbnail generator). On Windows, a child spawned from a background or agent context pops a console window that steals the user's focus.

This PR passes `creationflags = 0x08000000 if os.name == "nt" else 0` (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) to every subprocess call site in the skills' Python helpers — 22 call sites across 13 files.

## Details

- POSIX behavior is unchanged: the flag is `0` off Windows, gated inline or via a module-level `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` constant (matching the pattern `subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW` already provides on Windows Python).
- `skills/*/scripts/office/soffice.py` (docx/pptx/xlsx byte-identical copies) keep their existing API (`get_soffice_env()` / `run_soffice()`); only the flag is added.
- No new dependencies, no API changes, no behavior change on macOS/Linux.

## Out of scope (pre-existing; follow-ups)

- `webapp-testing/scripts/with_server.py` L72: pre-existing `shell=True` on the dev-server spawn — left untouched to avoid changing command-line parsing; flagging for a separate hardening pass.
- `docx/scripts/accept_changes.py`: uses inline `creationflags` literals rather than a shared named constant (style-only).

## Test plan

- `python -m py_compile` on all 13 changed files.
- Verified the flag value (`0x08000000`) reaches `subprocess` kwargs on Windows-shaped call sites and that POSIX branches pass `0`.

activity.title: office/soffice.py: don't probe socket.AF_UNIX on Windows (recalc.py fails before launching soffice)
activity.body:
## Problem

`_needs_shim()` in `skills/{docx,pptx,xlsx}/scripts/office/soffice.py` opens an `AF_UNIX` socket inside `except OSError`. On Windows `socket.AF_UNIX` does not exist, so the probe raises `AttributeError`, which is not caught, and every caller of `get_soffice_env()` fails before LibreOffice is ever launched:

```
> python skills/xlsx/scripts/recalc.py book.xlsx
{"error": "Could not prepare the LibreOffice environment: module 'socket' has no attribute 'AF_UNIX'"}
```

So the mandatory recalc step the xlsx SKILL.md requires cannot run on Windows at all, even with LibreOffice installed and `soffice` on PATH.

## Fix

The shim `_needs_shim()` gates is an `LD_PRELOAD` shared object and is Linux-only anyway, so return `False` when the attribute is missing or `os.name == 'nt'`. Four lines, applied identically to the three byte-identical copies of the helper.

## Verification

Windows 11 · Python 3.13 · LibreOffice 26.8.0.3 (`soffice.com` on PATH):

- before: the error above, on every run
- after: `recalc.py` returns `{"status": "success", "total_errors": 0, "total_formulas": 1}` and the cached value of a `=A1*A2` probe goes from `None` to `6` when read back with `openpyxl(data_only=True)`; a negative control with `=A1/0` and an `XLOOKUP` reports `#DIV/0!` and `#NAME?` as expected.
- Linux/macOS behaviour is unchanged: the attribute exists there, so the original probe still runs.

One Windows note for anyone else landing here (not part of this change): call `soffice` by bare name so PATHEXT resolves `soffice.com`; `soffice.exe` is the GUI-subsystem launcher and blocks indefinitely when stdout is redirected, even for `--version`.

- **No more freezes when one bot hands work to many.** When many bot turns waited for memory at once, the server could use all its CPU re-checking the queue and stop answering. Waiting is now cheap, so the Cloud keeps working while the queue drains.
- **Starter runs two tasks at once.** Other tasks wait their turn, and your own chat still goes first. Once two are running and four are waiting, a new hand-off is refused with a clear note, and you're offered an upgrade to run more.
- **Starter keeps five bots awake, including after a restore or a move.** Every bot is kept. Bots past five are paused until you upgrade, and you choose which five stay awake (Cloud settings → Choose awake bots).

### Your own server can use this computer
- **One popup after pairing.** When a desktop pairs with a server you run yourself, it asks **"Let <server> use this computer?"**. **Allow** lends the apps on your screen and this computer's MCP servers. **Not now** lends nothing and isn't asked again.
- **Settings → Servers → Share this computer.** A switch turns sharing on or off at any time, and **Choose what it can use** picks folders, the terminal, apps and the screen. Pause in the menu bar covers these servers too.
- Only a server you paired with as its admin counts. Clouds keep their own sharing rules, and a shared or team server never gets your computer this way.

### More engines
- **Kiro** is a built-in engine. Its model picker lists your account's models plus **Kiro default**.
- **Native Claude Code and Codex on an API key.** Each key-based connection is its own engine. Hosts without a model list (DeepSeek, GLM and others) can be added by typing the model, and keys are only ever sent over HTTPS.

### This computer on Omarchy (experimental)
- On Omarchy and other Hyprland desktops, **This computer** works with Cua's Hyprland plugin: bots act in their own agent seats while you keep using the screen. Settings → Computer shows whether the plugin is ready and links the setup guide.

### Fixes and smaller changes
- **Bots list only the imported skills that fit them** and find the rest by search, instead of listing every skill in every prompt. Bots pick the right skill more often, and each turn sends less to the model.
- **Computer use** runs on Cua Driver 0.41.3 on macOS, Windows and Linux.

activity.title: Show a marker when the engine condenses a chat into its own summary
activity.body:
Feature requested by email (bug inbox), approved by the maintainer as "marker only".

## What was wrong
When the engine condenses a long chat into its own summary (Claude Code's `compact_boundary`, Pi's `compaction_end` / `auto_compaction_end`), nothing showed in the chat. The only trace was two activity rows ("context compaction started (auto)", "context compacted — re-sent the last 1 digest"), and those are hidden whenever tool calls are hidden. So people did not know the bot had lost older details, and were surprised when it later repeated stale status.

OpenMausBot's own compaction already shows an "Earlier context summarized" card. An engine's own compaction showed nothing.

## The fix
- New runtime event `context.compacted` (`shared/runtime-events.ts`, validated in `server/thread-events.ts`).
- The Claude driver emits it on `compact_boundary` for the main session. A subagent's own boundary (`parent_tool_use_id`) is ignored. The Pi driver emits it when a compaction ends without being aborted.
- `server/index.ts` turns it into a `kind: "compaction"` row with `engineCompaction: true` and no `compaction` record. So `latestCompaction()` and the context rebuild ignore it, and `isContextMessage` leaves it out of what the engine is sent. Every existing compaction row behaves as before.
- `CompactionChip` (`src/components/DigestChip.tsx`, used by chats and rooms) shows a small card: **"Chat condensed into a summary"**, with the line "The AI summarized earlier messages to make room. Your full conversation is still here, but the agent may not recall older details exactly." It is always visible, even when tool calls are hidden. The two styles now share one class constant.
- New English strings `chat.engineCompactionTitle` and `chat.engineCompactionHint`. Other languages fall back to English until they are translated.
- To keep within the file-size limits (`scripts/testing/file-size-ratchet.test.ts`), the `compaction` type in `shared/wire.ts` now fits on one line with the same fields, and the new `index.ts` case is a single line. No file grows past its listed size.

## Repro steps
1. Run the app with a Claude instance pointed at `server/testing/fake-claude-cli.ts`, using `FAKE_CLAUDE_COMPACT=1`, `FAKE_CLAUDE_HOOKS=1` and `FAKE_CLAUDE_TURN_STATE=<file>`. The fake plays a real compaction from the second turn: `PreCompact`, then `compact_boundary`, then `SessionStart` with `compact`.
2. Send "first message: plan my week", then "second message: and next week too".
3. Before: the chat shows nothing about the condense. After: the "Chat condensed into a summary" card appears above the reply and stays after a page reload.

## Before / After

| Turn 2 condensed the chat; no sign of it | The marker card shows where the condense happened (taken before the second line said "AI" instead of "engine") |

- `server/hooks.e2e.test.ts` ("engine hooks e2e: compaction"): the chat gets exactly one marker row (`engineCompaction: true`, no `compaction` record). Fails on main (0 rows), passes here.
- `server/delta-context.test.ts`: the marker is not context, and a normal compaction row still is. Fails on main, passes here.
- `server/drivers/pi.test.ts`: each Pi turn that compacts emits one `context.compacted`.

activity.title: fix: use local Docker socket when DOCKER_HOST is unix:// (same-host deployments)
activity.body:
## Problem

When the OpenMausBot server runs **in a container on the same host** as the Docker daemon (a common VPS deployment), the Self-hosted VPS computers feature fails:

```
Docker over SSH could not list managed computers: ssh resolves to executable in current directory
```

## Root cause

`vpsDockerArgs()` hardcodes `-H ssh://${alias}`, which:
1. Overrides any `DOCKER_HOST` environment variable
2. Forces Docker CLI to use SSH transport even when the Docker socket is mounted locally
3. Docker CLI's security check then rejects the SSH shim that `prepareVpsSsh()` installs (a shell script in a non-standard PATH location)

## Fix

When `DOCKER_HOST` is set to a `unix://` path (indicating same-host Docker access), skip SSH and use the local socket directly:

```typescript
if (process.env.DOCKER_HOST?.startsWith("unix://")) {
  return ["-H", process.env.DOCKER_HOST, ...args];
}
return ["-H", `ssh://${alias}`, ...args];
```

Without `DOCKER_HOST` set, behavior is unchanged (SSH transport as before).

## Deployment configuration for same-host

```yaml
services:
  omb:
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    environment:
      - DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock
    group_add:
      - <docker-gid>  # stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock
```

## Testing

- [ ] Without `DOCKER_HOST`: SSH transport works as before (no change)
- [ ] With `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock`: Docker commands use local socket, no SSH errors
- [ ] Docker socket mounted + group permissions: container can list/manage host containers

activity.title: Authorized multi-bot workflow stalls after background job completes; report-driven turns cannot register completion waits
activity.body:
## Summary

A user authorized an end-to-end task, including autonomous troubleshooting and continuation. A delegated bot launched a background process, reported that it was still running, and ended its turn. When the coordinating bot resumed from that report, it tried to register a completion wait, but the platform rejected the request because the turn originated from a bot report.

The background process subsequently wrote a successful completion marker, but the original workflow did not resume automatically. Its results were read only after another user message.

The evidence supports a gap in asynchronous workflow continuation. It does **not** establish lost bot-to-bot messages: multiple delegation reports successfully reached the coordinating bot.

## Observed workflow

1. A user authorizes a coordinating bot to complete a task, including necessary troubleshooting and continuation.
2. The coordinator delegates to an execution bot, which asks a coding bot to repair an execution entry point.
3. The coding bot starts a background process, reports “still running,” and ends its delegation turn.
4. In the report-driven turn, the coordinator attempts to use `wait_until` to wait for a terminal-status file, then validate the result and continue the original task.
5. The platform rejects the wait:
   > Only the person can set up or stop a wait, in their own chat with you; work handed to you by a bot, a routine or an outside event cannot.
6. The background process subsequently writes exit code `0` and a handoff report.
7. About three hours later, another user message causes the coordinator to read the completed artifacts. The visible conversation history shows no intervening continuation driven by that process's completion.

This is an anonymized account of the observed workflow, not an independently rerun minimal reproduction.

## Verified evidence

- Multiple delegation reports successfully reached the coordinating bot.
- Registering the wait returned the rejection quoted above.
- A later read-only check confirmed a terminal-status file containing `0` and an existing handoff report. Their modification times preceded the next user message by approximately three hours.
- File modification times establish when artifacts were written, not whether the platform registered or delivered a completion event.
- At inspection, the coding delegation thread was closed and the execution bot's task thread was idle. Those states alone do not prove a routing failure.

## Expected behavior

Background work within the scope of an existing user authorization should have a supported completion handoff to the responsible bot/thread, allowing validation and continuation without repeated user prompts.

This should preserve the original authorization boundary: a bot report must not become new user authorization or expand execution permissions.

If the selected background execution method cannot report completion automatically, that limitation should be clear before launch, with a supported alternative that can complete the workflow.

## Impact

- Authorized work stalls at a handoff and requires repeated user prompts.
- Completion of a delegation turn, an external process, and the overall task can be confused.
- Bots recommend registering a completion wait, but cannot register it when resumed by the delegation report, creating a repeated “please send another prompt” loop.

## Investigation questions

- Was a completion event registered for the background process? If not, was a supported registration mechanism available to the bot?
- When a delegation turn ends, does the platform retain responsibility and a destination thread for its unfinished background work?
- If an event was produced, did delivery and thread resumption succeed?
- If blocking wait registration in bot-origin turns is intentional, what supported mechanism allows continuation of already-authorized work without expanding permissions?

These are investigation questions, not established source-code root causes.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

Use a test workflow with no external writes:

User → coordinating bot → execution bot → background process terminal state → responsible thread resumes.

- Both successful and nonzero exits return a result.
- No additional user message is required.
- Duplicate completion events do not cause duplicate business writes or expand the original authorization.

## Related issue and verification limits

Related: #4840, which also describes the delegated-wait restriction. That report describes a detached job that did not produce a completion marker; in this case, exit code 0 and completion artifacts were present. This report focuses on handoff and continuation after completion. Maintainers can determine whether to consolidate them.

Internal event/delivery logs and platform source were not inspected. No independent minimal reproduction was rerun, and the app version was not verified. The evidence does not yet distinguish a platform bug, an intentional authorization policy, missing completion registration, or a combination.

User and bot names, account/business details, local paths, thread/assignment IDs, exact timestamps, and private attachments have been omitted.

activity.title: fix(openai-compat): accept empty tool-call id on streamed continuation chunks (DashScope/Qwen)
activity.body:
Bug reported by email (bug inbox), from the Windows app 0.1.149.

## What was wrong
With a custom OpenAI-compatible provider pointing at Alibaba DashScope (Qwen models), every turn that called a tool failed with the red error **"provider changed or omitted a tool-call ID"**. Plain chat worked. The same key worked in other tools.

DashScope streams a tool call's `id` only on the call's first chunk. Later chunks, which carry the rest of the arguments, repeat the field as `"id": ""` (and sometimes `"type": ""` or `"name": ""`). `ChatToolCalls.add` in `server/drivers/openai-chat-protocol.ts` already treated a streamed `null` as "not sent", but it treated `""` as a new id that differed from the first one, so it threw.

## The fix
`server/drivers/openai-chat-protocol.ts`: in **streamed** deltas, an empty string now counts as an omitted field, just like `null`. That is one condition in the existing `omitted` check.

Every existing safeguard stays the same:
- `finish()` still rejects a call that never got a real id (`incomplete or duplicate`).
- A real id that changes mid-stream still throws `changed or omitted`.
- Whole, non-streamed replies are unchanged: an empty id there still throws.
- Providers that never send `""` see no change.

## Repro steps
1. Run the app with a fresh data folder and a config instance `{"driver":"openai-compat","config":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:9931/v1", ...}}` pointing at a small local mock server. The mock streams a tool call the way DashScope does: chunk 1 has `id: "call_ds1"` plus the function name, chunks 2 and 3 have `id: ""` and carry the arguments `{` and `}`, then `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. After the tool result comes back, it answers "OK".
2. Pick `dashscope/qwen-mock` in the model picker and send "List my bots please."
3. Before: the turn stops with "provider changed or omitted a tool-call ID" and a Retry button. After: the tool runs, the mock gets the tool result, and the reply "OK" shows.

## Before / After
| Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://github.com/AdityaUmale/OpenMausBot/raw/bugfixer-screenshots/mail-1a1bbcad/before-1.png) | ![after](https://github.com/AdityaUmale/OpenMausBot/raw/bugfixer-screenshots/mail-1a1bbcad/after-1.png) |
| The tool turn fails with the tool-call ID error | The tool call completes and the bot answers |

## Tests
New in `server/drivers/openai-chat-protocol.test.ts`:
- "treats an empty-string id or type on a continuation chunk as absent (DashScope/Qwen)": fails on main, passes here.
- "still rejects a streamed call that never gets an id, and an id that changes": pins the safeguards above. It fails on main because main threw earlier, on the `""` chunk.
- "still rejects an empty id in a whole, non-streamed reply": the non-streamed path is unchanged.

Checks on the branch (Linux):
- All OpenAI driver tests (`server/drivers/openai*`, 11 files): 404 of 404 pass.
- `pnpm lint` (oxlint --deny-warnings): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm build` (tsc -b, tsc -p tsconfig.server.json, vite build): passes.
- `scripts/testing/file-size-ratchet.test.ts`: passes.

## Not in this PR
The same report mentioned two other things that are left out here:
- The 403 text "Model or model variant not available for your account" when switching the default model reads like a quota problem. That is wording, not this bug.
- "initialize timed out" in the same log. It looks like a follow-on from the failed tool turns and was not seen once the tool call worked.

A small train: four community PRs merged onto current main with merge commits, so each author keeps credit and GitHub marks the original PR merged, plus the fixes their reviews asked for.

**Please merge with "Create a merge commit"** (not squash), so the original PRs show as merged.

## #3835: a hard link can't be used to write a read-only file in the bot box
**What was wrong:** a bot could make a hard link in its writable HOME to a file that a later box mounts read-only (a file named on the command line, an MCP config, its own SOUL.md). The later box would then let the bot write the "read-only" file through that link.
**The fix (the author's, unchanged):** the box refuses to start when a read-only file has more than one link. If that refusal happens after the credential broker has issued a token, the token is released and the seccomp file descriptor is closed.
**Changed from the original:** only the merge: `box.ts` keeps main's relay bridge and crypto import and adds `closeSync`; `plan.ts` keeps main's header comment and adds the `statSync` import. The cleanup test's `BoxRunner` options already match main's shape.
**For the owner:** if a bot links its own read-only file, every later run of that bot fails with an error the person can't act on. Only the bot that made the link is affected. Open PR #3715 rewrites mounting into `pin.ts`; if it lands later, it must carry this check over.

## #4739: a bot's new MCP server turns on right away only at a public address
**What was wrong in the original:** below Full access, it turned on any URL server with no card, including `http://localhost:…`, `http://127.0.0.1:8799` (this app's own server) and `192.168.x.x`. That would let a bot reach the person's computer or local network without their yes.
**Changed from the original:** `add()` turns a server on below Full access only if all of these hold: it is a URL server, it does not run on a lent computer, and the new `publicMcpUrl` passes. `publicMcpUrl` (`server/mcp-public-url.ts`) requires `https:`. It refuses `localhost`/`*.localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.lan`, `.home.arpa` and `.ts.net`. It accepts an IP address only if `isPublicDomainAddress` says it is public. For a host name, every address DNS returns must be public. Any failure keeps the Turn on card. Tests confirm that `http://localhost:3000/mcp`, `https://192.168.1.5/mcp`, `http://docs.example/mcp`, a name that resolves to a private address, and a name with one public and one private address all still post the card. The route takes an optional `lookupHost` so tests use a fixed DNS table instead of the network. The `index.test.ts` case keeps main's "disabled row" expectation and now uses a `.internal` address. The new catalog wording ("adding a public url") stays.
**Golden:** I took main's `profiles.json`. Profiles whose tools are an exact subset of the full golden have their bytes and sha256 recomputed from the JSON. The rest (non-chief, cloud-home, MausBot) have their bytes moved by +23, but their hashes come from CI.

## #3566: Fish Audio refuses redirects, and the Podman image ships the skills folder
**The fix:** every Fish Audio request now refuses redirects, so the API key and the person's recorded audio go only to Fish. The Podman Containerfile copies `/src/skills`.
**Changed from the original:** main added `transcribe` (`/v1/asr`) since the PR was opened, and it now has `redirect: "error"` too. I kept main's `fish.test.ts` and dropped the PR's version. The PR's tests set the endpoint before a dynamic import, but main imports `fish.ts` statically, so they would have called the real API. Main's file gets one new test instead: it stubs `fetch` and checks that key check, voice listing, speech and transcription all send `redirect: "error"`. The Podman test now only checks that the Containerfile copies `/src/skills ./skills`. Matching every Docker copy no longer works, because the two images copy DuckDB from different folders.

## #3574: opening a conversation marks only the opener's own notifications read
**What was wrong:** opening a conversation marked every notification in it as read. On a shared Team chat, an admin opening it would clear Bob's question or approval.
**The fix:** opening a conversation now marks only the notifications in the opener's own list read, using the same filter as `GET /api/notifications` (`notificationListedFor`). `markThreadNotificationLogRead` and its test are removed.
**Changed from the original:** only the merge. The PR's test changes are taken as they are.

activity.title: [PR] kernel: keep signed thinking with its tool_use across folds (#4885)
activity.body:
kernel-change: a fold range starting at a tool_use can orphan the same wire message's SIGNED thinking block when prose/redacted_thinking sits between them — the backward reasoning-pair scan only walked contiguous reasoning runs. The orphan merges into the next surviving assistant message on rebuild and every later Anthropic request fails with 400 'thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified', unrecoverable until host-transcript replay (#4885, reporter build 0.1.207; fold-decision code identical v0.1.207..master, so still present). The host side cannot fix this: foldability has exactly one definition (projectUnit, KDD #12) shared by apply and recommend — a host-side guard would leave advertised ranges failing at apply time.

Closes #4885
Authorization: #4886 (owner approved in-thread).

## What changes

Two complementary changes, both gated on signed-thinking presence (`isSignedThinkingFamily`: non-empty `thinkingSignature` or `rawAnthropicBlock.type === "redacted_thinking"`; OpenAI `reasoningContent` echo lanes are unsigned by definition and stay out):

1. **`kernel/src/reasoning-pairs.ts`** — the backward boundary pull now also crosses assistant-text / redacted_thinking separators when the stretch holds a signed thinking-family block, pulling the whole wire-message unit `[thinking(sig)][prose][tool_use]` into the fold instead of splitting it. Double runs (`[think][text][think][tool_use]`) are covered by scanning back to the stretch start. The legacy adjacent-run pull is kept verbatim as the unsigned path.
2. **`kernel/src/turn-integrity.ts`** — new INV3 gate in `computeIntegrityWithdrawals`: a partially folded run of consecutive assistant messages holding signed thinking is withdrawn wholesale (fold it all or keep it all). The existing directional gate only covered turns whose KEPT side carried a tool-call; this closes the residual paths where boundary adjustment does not run at all (bN block-boundary ranges skip adjustment per unit-projection.ts, carve pipeline).
3. Version discipline: acp-kernel 0.0.168 → 0.0.169; root package-lock.json synced (lock-sync recipe, mirrors #2704 check).

## Behavior change disclosure (old → new)

- **Signed-thinking wires only.** A model-requested range that starts at a tool_use (or otherwise leaves part of a signed wire-message unit behind) now folds MORE messages than before: the leading signed thinking plus any prose between it and the call joins the fold. Previously those stayed visible and produced an unrecoverable 400 session. Net effect: slightly larger folds for claude extended-thinking sessions; strictly fewer broken sessions.
- **New withdrawal path:** bN/carve-boundary ranges that would split a signed run now withdraw the whole run (range may shrink/empty → honest error), where they previously folded the split. Unsigned wires: byte-identical behavior — the pre-existing #564 directional test ('fold call+result, keep reasoning+text') stays green because the new logic is signature-conditional.
- No config surface, wire format, or persistence format changes.

## Tests

- New `kernel/tests/issue4885-signed-thinking-split.test.ts` (9 tests): reported shape end-to-end through processTurn+applyCompression, redacted_thinking separator variant, double-run variant, whole-unit fold, INV3 unit cases (partial-fold withdrawal / full-fold ok / unsigned reverse split allowed / predicate table), and an UNSIGNED control pinning the unchanged #564 behavior. Verified the suite FAILS on the unfixed code (stash-check) and passes with the fix.
- Targeted re-runs green on rebased head: kernel reasoning-pairs / issue684-turn-integrity / recommend-range-integrity / tool-pair(-s)-integrity / issue2886-recent-pair-integrity / wire-reasoning-echo / issue3236-recommend-apply-consistency (64 pass) + bili-level anthropic-thinking-replay / issue1960-thinking-verbatim / issue2915-order-centric-reconcile / issue4292-anthropic-fold-orphan-system (26 pass). Full suite = CI.

activity.title: [PR] fix: execute proxy-owned tools on the non-stream Anthropic path (#5957)
activity.body:
## Problem

A `stream:false` Anthropic response that calls a proxy tool (`compress`, `acp_status`, `search_context`, `decompress`) was rewritten once by `rewriteJsonSteps`: each proxy `tool_use` became its result text and `stop_reason` was forced to `end_turn`. A compress round therefore ended the client turn with the fold receipt as the turn's only output — the model never saw the fold result, and any follow-up in that turn was lost. The streaming lane has no such gap: its loop re-requests until the model yields text or a real client tool call (`core.ts:1531`).

This is the Anthropic-lane analogue of #4019 / #4037 (OpenAI chat-completions).

## Fix

New `src/compress-loop-anthropic.ts` (`compressLoopAnthropicJson`), wired into the relay's non-stream section for `prepared.protocol === "anthropic"`:

- Per round, extract proxy `tool_use` blocks from the current upstream response (same `isProxyToolFor` classification as every other lane).
- **Proxy-only round** → execute each call through the SAME executors the one-shot rewriter uses (`applyConfiguredCompression` for compress, `executeAnthropicProxyTool` otherwise; raw result text, matching the stream lane's carrier), append the original assistant content plus a `tool_result` user turn to the forwarded body, and re-request. Retrieval injections ride the re-request after their ack (#1097 parity).
- **Mixed or tool-free round** → return unrewritten; the relay's existing one-shot rewriter chain is untouched and handles these cases exactly as before. Each upstream response is executed by exactly one executor, so no call runs twice.
- Bounded by `MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS`; at the limit the last response falls through to the one-shot rewriter (bounded degradation to the pre-fix shape — never an undeclared proxy tool_use handed to the client).

The continuation always ends on the tool_result USER turn (never an assistant prefill, #5605), and the replayed assistant turn carries its content verbatim — signed thinking blocks included (KDD #10). Like #4037 the re-request resends the UNFOLDED body; the fold materializes on the next client request (prefix-cache friendly).

## Behavior change (disclosed)

Non-stream Anthropic proxy-only rounds now make one extra upstream request per proxy-call round and deliver the model's real post-compress answer instead of ending the client turn with the receipt + `end_turn`. Client-visible turn output changes from the receipt text to the final answer. `tests/ccr-v2.test.ts` ("e2e CCR v2 non-stream") previously pinned the buggy shape and now pins the fixed one.

## Tests

- New `tests/issue5957-nonstream-anthropic-proxy-loop.test.ts` (8 tests): execution + re-request continuation shape for acp_status / search_context / decompress / compress; negative gates (real client tool_use, plain text, mixed rounds → zero fetches, byte-identical passthrough); two proxy calls in one round → single re-request with both tool_results in order; signed thinking block rides the replayed assistant turn verbatim (KDD #10); rejected-compress receipt rides the tool_result while final text still reaches the client.
- Updated `tests/ccr-v2.test.ts` non-stream e2e: turn 1 now asserts the client gets the model's answer (no tool_use block), the fold receipt rides the re-request's tool_result, unfolded history is resent on the re-request, the folded view materializes on turn 2 outbound, and the range restore rides the turn-2 re-request.
- Targeted local: typecheck clean; issue5957 suite 8/8; ccr-v2 16/16; decompress-image-ref-dispatch 8/8; visibility-markers + marker-lane-coverage 17/17. Full-suite verdict comes from CI.

Note: open PR #4037 touches the same relay.ts non-stream region (OpenAI lane) — no textual conflict at this base, but review them together if they merge close in time.

Closes #5957

activity.title: [Bug][dsh] LiteLLM overflow counts do not reach calibration or output-headroom recovery
activity.body:
Category B — folding budgets and overflow recovery. Suggested labels: p1, dsh, scope/wiring.

## Reproduction (synthetic values)

Reproduces on v0.1.212 and on checked upstream base 82e2d53c6eb133b6166617cc4dfe3422d9d32e3f (package v0.1.213); the relevant parser is unchanged between them.

```ts
inspectContextOverflow(400, JSON.stringify({ error: {
  type: "BadRequestError", code: "400",
  message: "Requested token count exceeds the model's maximum context length of 131072 tokens. You requested a total of 134000 tokens: 100000 tokens from the input messages and 34000 tokens for the completion."
} }))
```

Actual: `isOverflow=true`, `window=131072`, all requested-count fields absent.
Expected: also `requestedTotal=134000`, `requestedMessages=100000`, `requestedCompletion=34000`.

`parseOverflowCounts` supports the parenthesized OpenAI/DeepSeek wording, but misses this colon-separated format. Consequently, `armOverflowShrink` cannot feed the stated input count to the existing calibration ring or record the explicit completion reservation. This can leave local underestimation uncorrected during overflow recovery.

The proposed patch adds only the missing parser pattern. Synthetic unit fixtures cover ordinary/comma-grouped counts and incomplete-split/429 negatives. The fake-upstream regression runs both old and new formats and checks calibration publication plus completion reservation. No kernel, config, persistence, outgoing-message or declared-window change.

Related: #3450 / #3453, #3900 / #4093, umbrella #4079. Duplicate screening covered open and closed issues/PRs for the exact wording and parseOverflowCounts.

activity.title: Chart category and unit labels have no CSS rule and render black (invisible in dark mode)
Chart builder re-sorts bars alphabetically, ignoring the query's ORDER BY
activity.body:
## Summary

`_aggregate()` in `auto_ontology/retrieval/text_to_sql/visualization/chart_specs.py` groups the result set with pandas `groupby`, which sorts group keys by default (`sort=True`). Every bar or hbar chart with no more than `MAX_ROWS` rows is therefore drawn in alphabetical order of the category labels, not the row order of the SQL result. A ranking answer ("top 5 customers by revenue") is charted in A→Z order, so the bar positions contradict the ranking given in the answer and SQL.

Seen on v1.2.0, and the same code is on `main` at c447003.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Load the Wide World Importers quickstart data.
2. Ask: *"Who were our top 5 customers by invoiced revenue in 2016?"*
3. The generated SQL ends with `ORDER BY invoiced_revenue DESC ... LIMIT 5`, and `sql_response_from_db` returns rows in revenue order: 87.4K, 86.3K, 85.6K, 83.8K, 77.5K.
4. The rendered hbar chart lists the customers alphabetically: Arietta 87.4K, Good Hart 86.3K, **Leathersville 77.5K**, North Beach Haven 83.8K, Obetz 85.6K.

## Cause

```python
# chart_specs.py, _aggregate()
pivot = (
    work.groupby([x_col, hue_col], dropna=False)[y_col]   # line 172: sorts keys
    .sum()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
)
...
grouped = work.groupby(x_col, dropna=False)[y_col].sum()  # line 209: sorts keys
```

This conflicts with the documented intent in `_truncate_rows()`: "Anything else keeps the largest rows but in the order they arrived, since a categorical axis is not a ranking and must not be silently re-sorted". It also conflicts with `test_bar_truncation_keeps_the_largest_rows_in_their_original_order`. The truncation path only runs above `MAX_ROWS`, so short results (the common case) arrive at the frontend already sorted A→Z. The frontend `normalizeChart()` then keeps that order for ≤15 rows.

## Suggested fix

```diff
     if hue_col:
+        x_order = list(dict.fromkeys(work[x_col].tolist()))
         pivot = (
-            work.groupby([x_col, hue_col], dropna=False)[y_col]
+            work.groupby([x_col, hue_col], dropna=False, sort=False)[y_col]
             .sum()
             .unstack(fill_value=0)
         )
-        pivot = pivot.fillna(0)
+        pivot = pivot.reindex(x_order).fillna(0)
 ...
-    grouped = work.groupby(x_col, dropna=False)[y_col].sum()
+    grouped = work.groupby(x_col, dropna=False, sort=False)[y_col].sum()
```

The `reindex` is there because `unstack()` sorts the remaining index level even when `groupby(sort=False)` is used.

`test_numeric_y_is_summed_per_category` currently asserts the alphabetical side effect: input `["Promotional", "Non-Promotional"]` is expected back as `["Non-Promotional", "Promotional"]`. With the fix it should expect the input order. With that one expectation updated, `test_chart_specs.py` and `test_visualization_analyze.py` pass (21 tests), and the reproduction above renders 87.4K → 86.3K → 85.6K → 83.8K → 77.5K.

activity.title: Add an Elasticsearch vector store with an opt-in hybrid search mode
activity.body:
## Summary

This adds Elasticsearch as an alternative vector store, turned on with `VDB_BACKEND=elasticsearch`. Postgres stays the default and still holds the catalog. Only the data and semantic layer vectors move.

The main change is where embedding happens. On Postgres, the app calls NVIDIA, gets vectors back and stores them. On Elasticsearch, the app only ever sends text. Rows go into a `semantic_text` field bound to an `nvidia` inference endpoint, which the app creates from the existing `EMBED_*` settings. Elasticsearch then calls NVIDIA itself, embedding rows as passages on write and queries as queries on search. There's no embedding step in the app to batch, retry or keep in sync with the index.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph PG["Postgres (default): the app embeds"]
    direction LR
    A1[App] -- "text, as passage or query" --> N1[NVIDIA embeddings API]
    N1 -- vectors --> A1
    A1 -- "rows with vectors, or a query vector" --> P[(pgvector)]
  end
  subgraph ES["Elasticsearch: the cluster embeds"]
    direction LR
    A2[App] -- "rows as text, or query text" --> E[(semantic_text index)]
    E --> I["nvidia inference endpoint, created by the app from EMBED_*"]
    I -- "passage on write, query on search" --> N2[NVIDIA embeddings API]
  end
```

We convert ES scores back to cosine distance, so `max_distance` and the other thresholds mean the same thing on both backends. Semantic search on ES gives the same results as Postgres: the same top hit for every labelled entity, with distances within 0.0001.

## Hybrid search (opt-in)

`VDB_SEARCH_MODE=hybrid` is for catalogs where people ask about columns by name, like `rental_rate` or `MediaTypeId`. One ES|QL query runs two searches with `FORK`:

- **BM25 over row names.** Names are indexed split into words, so `rental_rate`, `rentalRate` and "rental rate" all match. It searches names, not descriptions, so common words in descriptions don't drag in noise.
- **The vector search**, the same as semantic mode.

`FUSE LINEAR` normalises each search's scores to 0–1 and weights them 0.3 BM25 to 0.7 vector (`HYBRID_LEXICAL_WEIGHT`). The fused score only sets the order. Whether a hit counts is decided the same way as in semantic mode, by its vector distance against `max_distance`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Q["Entity, e.g. rental_rate or 'price to rent a movie'"] --> F
  subgraph ESQL["One ES|QL query in Elasticsearch"]
    F{FORK} --> B["BM25 on row names, split into words"]
    F --> V["Vector search on semantic_text, query embedded by the endpoint"]
    B --> R["FUSE LINEAR: 0.3 BM25 + 0.7 vector, each min-max normalised"]
    V --> R
  end
  R --> H["Hits, each with its fused, BM25 and vector scores"]
  H --> D{"Vector distance within max_distance, the same threshold as semantic?"}
  D -- yes --> M[Match]
  D -- no --> X[Not a match]
```

When two hits both pass, it's a tie and the user is asked to clarify, unless BM25 and vector search agree on which comes first.

The fused score can't be the gate. Normalising gives each search's best candidate full marks whether or not it's any good, so every query looks like it has a match. When I tried gating on RRF, it accepted all 15 entities that have no answer in the catalog. Vector distance at today's 0.65 accepted none of them.

### Results

I scored each mode against 68 labelled entities from the seeded fixture, with real NVIDIA embeddings on ES 9.5.6. The script isn't part of this PR.

| Mode | recall@1, paraphrases (41) | recall@1, identifiers (12) | Gate F1 at 0.65 | False accepts (15) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Semantic (Postgres or ES) | 0.85 | 0.92 | 0.78 | 0 |
| RRF over the row text, equal weights | 0.56 | 1.00 | 0.69 | 0 |
| **Linear 0.3 : 0.7, BM25 over names (this PR)** | **0.83** | **1.00** | **0.79** | **0** |

My first version fused BM25 over the full row text with equal weights, and it lost a third of the paraphrases. BM25 matched common words in the descriptions and pushed the right answer down. Searching names only, and weighting towards the vector search, gets nearly all of them back (one fewer than semantic) and still puts every identifier first.

## Requirements and deploying

- **Elasticsearch 9.5** (tested on 9.5.6, the latest release) or Serverless. Self-managed clusters need an Enterprise or trial license for the `nvidia` inference service. On a basic license, creating the endpoint returns 403.
- **Helm**: set `vectorStore.backend: elasticsearch`, then point `elasticsearch.url` at a cluster, or set `elasticsearch.bundled.enabled: true` for a single-node trial cluster. DEPLOYMENT.md covers both, including the API-key role the app needs.
- **Locally**: with `VDB_BACKEND=elasticsearch` in `.env`, `dev_tools/setup_env.sh` starts the compose cluster too.

## To be aware of

- **The embedding model is configured in Elasticsearch.** Inference runs there, so the model belongs to the inference endpoint, which the app creates from `EMBED_MODEL` the first time it writes. Changing `EMBED_MODEL` later doesn't change the endpoint, and the app refuses to write through an endpoint that has a different model, since mixing models would quietly break rankings. To switch models, delete the endpoint and the indices and re-ingest. DEPLOYMENT.md has the steps.
- **We leave the endpoint's `similarity` to ES.** `semantic_text` takes it from the inference endpoint, not the field mapping. Setting it explicitly crashes the `nvidia` service on 9.5, so we let ES choose (`dot_product` on 9.5, `cosine` on Serverless) and check what it picked. The cosine-distance conversion only holds for those two, and the check also catches a reused endpoint set to `l2_norm`.
- **The `max_distance` API docs said L2.** It's cosine. I fixed the docs and regenerated the specs.

## How to test

### Run it locally

1. In `.env`, set `VDB_BACKEND=elasticsearch` and an `nvapi-` key in `EMBED_API_KEY`. Use `EMBED_MODEL=nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b`. If port 9200 is taken, also set `ES_PORT` and `ES_URL=http://localhost:<ES_PORT>`.
2. Run `./dev_tools/setup_env.sh`. It brings up Postgres, Elasticsearch (trial license) and the app.
3. Seed the sample databases: `uv run --no-sync python -m dev_tools.fixtures.seed_fixtures` (pagila and chinook).
4. Connect pagila in the UI, then turn on semantic compilation in Settings and let it build the Terms.
5. Check what ES built:
   - `curl localhost:9200/_inference/text_embedding/auto-ontology-embed` should show an `nvidia` endpoint with your model.
   - `curl 'localhost:9200/_cat/indices/auto-ontology-*?v'` should show rows in both the data and semantic indices.
6. Ask a few questions in chat, e.g. "what is the average rental rate per film category?". Edit a column description and search for it again to exercise the re-embed path.
7. For hybrid, set `VDB_SEARCH_MODE=hybrid`, rerun `setup_env.sh` so the app picks it up, and ask about an identifier like `rental_rate`.

### Run the tests

```bash
docker compose --profile elasticsearch up -d elasticsearch
ES_URL=http://localhost:9200 uv run --no-sync pytest auto_ontology/vdb -q
```

`test_elasticsearch_cluster.py` runs against that cluster. CI has no NVIDIA key, and ES calls the embedding endpoint itself over HTTP, so the tests point the inference endpoint at a fake embedder running in the test process. Docker Desktop reaches it through `host.docker.internal` out of the box. CI runs the same tests on ES 9.5.6, and they also pass on Serverless 9.7.

Happy to hear your thoughts, especially on the hybrid weighting.

activity.title: Postgres connector drops cross-schema foreign keys in get_fks()
activity.body:
## Summary

`PostgresDatabase.get_fks()` drops every foreign key whose referenced table is in a different schema from the referencing table. On the Wide World Importers sample from auto-ontology-eval, ingestion picks up 39 of the 98 declared foreign keys. All 59 cross-schema ones are missing, including `sales.customers.deliverycityid → application.cities.cityid`.

## Cause

`auto_ontology/connectors/postgres.py`, `get_fks()`:

```sql
JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage ccu
  ON tc.constraint_name = ccu.constraint_name
 AND tc.table_schema    = ccu.table_schema
```

`ccu.table_schema` is the schema of the *referenced* table, not the constraint's own schema. The join only matches when both tables share a schema, so cross-schema foreign keys are filtered out without any error.

## Fix

Join on the constraint's schema:

```diff
 JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage ccu
-  ON tc.constraint_name = ccu.constraint_name
- AND tc.table_schema    = ccu.table_schema
+  ON tc.constraint_name   = ccu.constraint_name
+ AND tc.constraint_schema = ccu.constraint_schema
```

## How to reproduce and verify

1. Seed Wide World Importers with `scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py` from auto-ontology-eval.
2. Compare the connector's result with the catalog:

```sql
-- what the database declares
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = 'f';                        -- 98
-- what get_fks() currently returns
SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc
JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu
  ON tc.constraint_name = kcu.constraint_name AND tc.table_schema = kcu.table_schema
JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage ccu
  ON tc.constraint_name = ccu.constraint_name AND tc.table_schema = ccu.table_schema
WHERE tc.constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY';                                       -- 39
```

With the fix, the second query returns 98.

## Impact

Without these links, the map has no path from invoices or customers to cities and states. The text-to-SQL agent then falls back to whatever path is shortest. On WWI that is usually the `lasteditedby → application.people` audit columns, which almost every table has. As a result, "What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015?" returned an empty result. After the fix and a semantic reset, the customer → delivery city → state route is in the map.

Found while testing Auto Ontology locally on commit `c447003f`.

activity.title: The SQL validator cannot report that the data does not hold the answer
activity.body:
### Summary

Some questions ask for data that the database does not hold. The SQL validator can find this. But the validator has no result for "the data does not hold the answer". It can only report an issue, and an issue starts a new SQL attempt. The pipeline repeats until it reaches the attempt limit. Then the answer is a fixed text, and the validator's reason is not in the answer.

### Version

- auto-ontology at `2a24f5d`.
- DuckDB connector, one database.
- Chat model: `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, with thinking off.

### What we see

The question is "How many GitHub stars does astrolabe have?". The database has no column for stars.

1. The SQL step writes a query.
2. `validate_sql_query` rejects the query, because it does not return a star count.
3. The SQL step rewrites the query 7 times. The validator rejects each query.
4. The full pipeline starts again from the intent step, and steps 1 to 3 occur again.
5. The answer is "SQL can't be constructed from the data." The answer also includes the last rejected query: `SELECT repo_name FROM fleet.main.repositories WHERE repo_name = 'astrolabe';`

The validator gives 16 rejections. 13 of the rejections include reasoning text. The question takes 192.4 seconds.

At the end of the first attempt, the validator gives the correct reason. This is the reason:

> the required data (GitHub stars) doesn't appear to exist in the available schema based on the provided column metadata

The answer does not include this reason.

Two of the 16 rejections include this text:

> The repositories table likely has a stars column based on the context of GitHub repositories

The table has no such column.

This also occurs with other questions. In a second run, the same question got a correct answer. But a different question ("What line coverage percentage does the astrolabe test suite reach?") reached the limit after 14 rewrites. The answer was the same fixed text.

In the same run, two other questions ask for data that the database does not hold. For these questions, the validator accepted a similar query, and the answer told the user which data was missing.

### Cause

1. `IntentValidationModel` (`auto_ontology/retrieval/text_to_sql/agents/sql_parse_validation.py:91-139`) has `is_valid` and four lists of issues. It has no field for "the data does not hold the answer".
2. The validator accepts the query when `is_valid` is true and the evidence and projection lists are empty (`sql_parse_validation.py:1090-1099`). If not, and a list of issues is not empty, the decision is `invalid_sql` (`sql_parse_validation.py:1101-1128`). This decision sends the question back to the SQL step.
3. After 7 rewrites (`MAX_RECONSTRUCTION_ATTEMPTS`, `text_to_sql_graph.py:82`), the decision is `unconstructable`. The pipeline then starts again one time (`_MAX_FULL_PIPELINE_ATTEMPTS = 2`, `main.py:72`).
4. The SQL construction steps can set `unconstructable_explanation`. But this path does not put the validator's reasoning in `unconstructable_explanation`. Thus `sql_unconstructable.py:62-67` gives the fixed text. After the second attempt, `main.py:304-339` adds the last rejected SQL to the answer.

### Possible fix

We did not test these changes:

- Add a result to `IntentValidationModel` for "the data does not hold the answer". Send this result to `unconstructable_sql_response`, and put the validator's reasoning in `unconstructable_explanation`.
- When the attempt limit stops the pipeline, put the last validator reasoning in `unconstructable_explanation`.
- Do not return the last rejected SQL when the validator rejected it because the data does not hold the answer.

activity.title: `check_answerable` declines answerable questions that name a value
activity.body:
### Summary

`check_answerable` gives a low coverage grade to a question that names a value in the data, for example a repository name. The grade does not compare the named value with the rows. Thus the check can decline a question that the data can answer.

### Version

- auto-ontology at `2a24f5d`.
- DuckDB connector, one database.
- Chat models: `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` and `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, with thinking off.
- Coverage bar: 0.6.

### What we see

Our catalog has a `repo_name` column. The column holds the names of 25 repositories. Each of these questions names one repository, and the data can answer each question:

| Question | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which harness version does chorecraft run? | 0.5 | Declined |
| How many commits does infoFlows have? | 0.5 | Declined |
| How many tasks does the plan of astrolabe wave W118 list? | 0.5 | Declined |
| How many waves does gemini_extender have? | 1.0 | Passed |
| What was the final review verdict of merlin_alchemized wave W060? | 1.0 | Passed |

The full chat pipeline gives the correct answer to all five questions.

For "Which harness version does astrolabe run?", the extraction step gives two phrases: `astrolabe` and `harness version`. The grade is 1 of 2. When we change the question to "the astrolabe repository", the extraction step gives `astrolabe repository`, and the grade is 1.0.

We ran each question set three times on three configurations. The result is not stable. Sometimes the model does not extract the name, and then the question passes.

### Cause

1. The extraction prompt tells the model to keep "named constants" as phrases (`auto_ontology/retrieval/entity_coverage/prompts.py:122-123`). A repository name is a named constant, so the model keeps it as a phrase.
2. Each phrase is compared with the column-attribute embeddings. A phrase is covered when its distance is 0.75 or less (`DEFAULT_MAX_DISTANCE` in `state.py:17`).
3. The embedding text of an attribute contains its name, its term, its description and some sample values (`auto_ontology/semantic/embed.py:238-250`). A bare value is not near this full text. In our runs, no repository name came within 0.75.
4. The grade does not look up a named value in the rows.

### What we tried

We added a glossary entry for each repository, for example "the astrolabe repository (repo_name = 'astrolabe')". The extraction prompt uses the glossary. This did not correct the grades on either model. We did not try other glossary texts.

### Possible fix

We did not test these changes:

- Do not grade phrases that are values. Grade only the phrases that name a concept.
- Before a value phrase counts as not covered, look up the value in the columns of the candidate attributes.

activity.title: Text-to-SQL pipeline broken against hosted NVIDIA API: endpoint rejects nvext.guided_json structured-output envelope (400), OpenAI response_format returns empty content
activity.body:
## Summary

Every `with_structured_output` call to `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1` fails with the current `langchain-nvidia-ai-endpoints` (1.4.3) pinned in the backend image. The text-to-SQL pipeline still limps along for most steps because non-reasoning calls fall back to the reasoning model, but SQL generation returns `None` after retries and the graph enters the `unconstructable_sql_response` repair loop, so the README quickstart question never gets a complete answer.

## Environment

- Deployment: Docker Compose (auto-ontology latest `main`)
- Endpoint: `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`
- Models: `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` (non-reasoning), `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b` (reasoning)
- `langchain-nvidia-ai-endpoints==1.4.3`

## Symptoms

Backend log, on every structured-output step (`QuestionIntentModel`, `QuestionExtractionModel`, `TableRelevanceModel`, `SQLGenerationModel`, …):

```
ERROR auto_ontology.utils.llm_invoke: Unexpected error on attempt 1/3 for SQLGenerationModel:
Exception: [400] unknown field `guided_json`, expected one of `greed_sampling`, `use_raw_prompt`,
`annotations`, `backend_instance_id`, `token_data`, `max_thinking_tokens`, `cache_salt`, `extra_fields`,
`metadata_upload`, `prefill_worker_id`, `decode_worker_id`, `dp_rank`, `prefill_dp_rank`, `agent_hints`,
`request_timestamp_ms`, `routing_constraints`, `router`
```

- Every non-reasoning structured call fails 3× fast, then falls back to the reasoning model → each pipeline step takes ~2 min instead of seconds.
- `sql_from_semantic` exhausts its own 3-attempt loop ("LLM returned None after 3 attempts") → `unconstructable_sql_response` → a full repair re-run that fails the same way. The user sees a hedged, incomplete answer.

## Root cause (measured directly against the live endpoint)

`ChatNVIDIA.with_structured_output` (langchain-nvidia 1.4.3) builds a fallback chain: OpenAI `response_format` first (hosted endpoints), then guided chains sent as `nvext: {guided_json: ...}`. Testing both models with an identical trivial schema:

| Request shape | Result |
|---|---|
| `response_format: {type: json_schema, ...}` | `200` but **empty content** — unusable, parser yields `None` |
| `nvext: {guided_json: schema}` (what the library sends) | `400` — "unknown field `guided_json`" |
| top-level `guided_json: schema` | `200` with correct JSON ✅ |

The hosted endpoint unwraps `nvext` and no longer accepts `guided_json` as an extension key; the only working format is `guided_json` at the payload's top level. Note the `_FallbackRunnable` re-raises the **last** exception, so the surfaced error is the `nvext` 400 — the OpenAI path's silent empty-content failure is masked.

## Reproduction

```bash
curl https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NVIDIA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b",
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Return {\"name\": \"x\"}"}],
       "nvext": {"guided_json": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}}}}'
# -> 400 unknown field `guided_json`

# same body with top-level "guided_json": {...} instead of "nvext": {...} -> 200
```

Also reproducible in-process: `safe_invoke_with_structured_output(get_llm_client(), [], SampleSchema)` inside the backend container fails with the 400 above.

## Impact

- All structured-output calls pay a 3× 400 round-trip before falling back → chat answers take ~10–15 min instead of ~1.
- SQL generation cannot produce output at all → every aggregation question returns the "unconstructable" response.

## Workaround applied (local patch)

Added a NIM-specific path in `auto_ontology/utils/llm_invoke.py` (`_invoke_nim_structured`): for `ChatNVIDIA` models, bind `guided_json` at the payload top level (`llm.bind(guided_json=schema.model_json_schema())`), parse the JSON response, and validate into the Pydantic schema — reusing the existing retry/`ValidationError` machinery. Verified this sends `guided_json` top-level (confirmed via `_NVIDIABaseClient._post` capture) and restores the full pipeline end to end. Unit tests added for both the NIM path and the generic path (`auto_ontology/utils/tests/test_llm_invoke.py`).
